        From c577f4a5a08bb9677e12ddafb62e2f3a901de87f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Mar 2019 15:09:10 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] PCI: rockchip: Fix rockchip_pcie_ep_assert_intx() bitwise
 operations

Currently the bitwise operations on the u16 variable 'status' with
the setting ROCKCHIP_PCIE_EP_CMD_STATUS_IS are incorrect because
ROCKCHIP_PCIE_EP_CMD_STATUS_IS is 1UL<<19 which is wider than the
u16 variable.

Fix this by making status a u32.

Fixes: cf590b078391 ("PCI: rockchip: Add EP driver for Rockchip PCIe controller")
Signed-off-by: Colin Ian King <colin.king@canonical.com>
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Pieralisi <lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Mukesh Ojha <mojha@codeaurora.org>
Acked-by: Shawn Lin <shawn.lin@rock-chips.com>
---
 drivers/pci/controller/pcie-rockchip-ep.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-rockchip-ep.c b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-rockchip-ep.c
index a5d799e2dff2..d743b0a48988 100644
--- a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-rockchip-ep.c
+++ b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-rockchip-ep.c
@@ -350,7 +350,7 @@ static void rockchip_pcie_ep_assert_intx(struct rockchip_pcie_ep *ep, u8 fn,
 	struct rockchip_pcie *rockchip = &ep->rockchip;
 	u32 r = ep->max_regions - 1;
 	u32 offset;
-	u16 status;
+	u32 status;
 	u8 msg_code;
 
 	if (unlikely(ep->irq_pci_addr != ROCKCHIP_PCIE_EP_PCI_LEGACY_IRQ_ADDR ||
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug was the incorrect use of a 16-bit unsigned integer (`u16`) to perform bitwise operations with a constant (`ROCKCHIP_PCIE_EP_CMD_STATUS_IS`) that is defined as a 32-bit value (`1UL<<19`). This mismatch in data types led to potential data loss and incorrect behavior during the operations, as the `u16` type could not accommodate the higher bit positions being manipulated. The fix involved changing the type of the `status` variable from `u16` to `u32` to ensure that it could properly handle the bitwise operations without truncation.

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the incorrect use of a 16-bit unsigned integer (`u16`) to perform bitwise operations with a constant (`ROCKCHIP_PCIE_EP_CMD_STATUS_IS`) that is defined as a 32-bit value (`1UL<<19`). This mismatch in data types led to potential data loss and incorrect behavior during the operations, as the `u16` type could not accommodate the higher bit positions being manipulated. The fix involved changing the type of the `status` variable from `u16` to `u32` to ensure that it could properly handle the bitwise operations without truncation.
